questions.question: A number line runs from 0 to 1 and is divided into 1000 equal steps, so one step is 0.001. Point A sits 600 steps from 0, which is 0.6. Point B sits 512 steps from 0, which is 0.512. Which statement is true?
options: A is farther right, so 0.6 > 0.512
B is farther right, so 0.512 > 0.6, because 0.512 has more digits
B is farther right, because 512 thousandths is more than 6 thousandths
A and B land on the same point, because 0.600 and 0.512 both have 3 digits after the point
questions.explain: Give both numbers the same number of decimal places first: 0.6 = 0.600, so 600 steps beats 512 steps and 0.6 > 0.512. The trap is thinking a longer-looking decimal is bigger.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0.25 to 0.26 and is divided into 10 equal parts, so each step is 0.001. Point M sits 4 steps to the right of 0.25, at 0.254. The right-hand end of the line is 0.26. Which statement is true?
options: 0.254 > 0.26, because 254 is bigger than 26
0.254 < 0.26, because M is still to the left of the end of the line, and 0.26 = 0.260
0.254 = 0.26, because both numbers sit between 0.25 and 0.26
0.254 > 0.26, because thousandths are worth more than hundredths
questions.explain: Rewrite 0.26 as 0.260 thousandths, then compare 254 with 260: point M has not reached the end of the line, so 0.254 < 0.26. The trap is comparing 254 with 26 as if the decimal point were not there.

questions.question: On a number line from 0 to 1 divided into 1000 equal steps of 0.001, point R is 400 steps from 0 (0.4), point S is 375 steps from 0 (0.375), and point T is 380 steps from 0 (0.38). Reading the line from left to right, which order are the three numbers in?
questions.explain: Write every number to thousandths first: 0.375, 0.380, 0.400, so left to right the order is 0.375, 0.38, 0.4. The trap is putting 0.4 last or first based on how many digits it has instead of how far along the line it sits.

questions.question: A number line runs from 2.5 to 2.6 and is divided into 100 equal parts, so each step is 0.001. Kai puts a marker 8 steps to the right of 2.5, at 2.508. Mia puts her marker at 2.51. Whose marker is farther to the right?
options: Kai's, because 2.508 has more digits than 2.51
Kai's, because 508 thousandths is more than 51 thousandths
Neither, because 2.508 and 2.51 land on the same point
Mia's, because 2.51 is the same as 2.510, and 510 thousandths is more than 508 thousandths
questions.explain: Fill 2.51 out to thousandths as 2.510, then compare 508 steps with 510 steps: Mia is 2 steps farther right. The trap is thinking the longer-looking decimal 2.508 must be the bigger one.

questions.question: Which one of these comparisons is TRUE?
questions.explain: Line the numbers up to the same place value before deciding: 0.600 > 0.589 is true, while 0.507 < 0.570, 0.081 < 0.180 and 0.25 < 0.30. The trap is thinking that more digits after the point means a bigger number.

questions.question: Four students ran the 60 m dash at a Burnaby track meet. Their times were: Ava 9.8 s, Ben 9.75 s, Cam 9.708 s, Dee 9.7 s. Who ran the SLOWEST time, that is, the greatest number of seconds?
options: Ben, 9.75 s
Ava, 9.8 s
Dee, 9.7 s
Cam, 9.708 s
questions.explain: Write all four times to thousandths: 9.800, 9.750, 9.708, 9.700, so the greatest time is Ava's 9.8 s. The trap is picking 9.708 or 9.75 because they look longer, when the tenths digit already decides it.

questions.question: At a Kamloops bulk food bin, Nina scoops 0.6 kg of oats and Sam scoops 0.58 kg. Which method and result are both correct?
options: Ignore the decimal points and compare 6 with 58, so 0.58 > 0.6
Count the digits after the point; 0.58 has more, so 0.58 > 0.6
Write both with the same number of decimal places, 0.600 and 0.580, then compare: 0.6 > 0.58
Add a zero at the front to get 0.06 and 0.58, then compare, so 0.58 > 0.6
questions.explain: Make the decimals the same length by writing zeros on the RIGHT (0.600 and 0.580), then compare place by place: 0.6 > 0.58. Adding zeros on the right never changes a decimal's value, but counting digits or adding a zero at the front does change it.

questions.question: Jayden measures how many litres of water are in four bottles: 3.07 L, 3.7 L, 3.007 L and 3.077 L. Ordered from GREATEST to LEAST, the amounts are:
questions.explain: Rewrite each amount to thousandths: 3.700, 3.077, 3.070, 3.007, then order from greatest down. The trap is starting with 3.077 because it looks the longest, or writing the list from least to greatest by mistake.

questions.question: Mrs. Chan's class can put a rock on the display shelf only if its mass is LESS THAN 1.2 kg. Rock A is 1.208 kg, rock B is 1.19 kg, rock C is 1.23 kg and rock D is 1.2 kg. Which rock or rocks can go on the shelf?
options: Only rock B (1.19 kg)
None of them, because 1.19 and 1.208 are both more than 1.2
Rocks A and B (1.208 kg and 1.19 kg)
Rocks B and D (1.19 kg and 1.2 kg)
questions.explain: Write every mass to thousandths and compare with 1.200: 1.190 < 1.200, while 1.208, 1.230 are greater and 1.200 is equal, not less, so only rock B fits. The traps are thinking 1.19 is more than 1.2 because it has more digits, and letting the equal value 1.2 count as 'less than'.

questions.question: Priya says that 0.125 is greater than 0.13 because 125 is greater than 13. Which statement best explains her thinking?
options: She is right; a decimal with more digits is always the bigger one.
She compared the digits without lining up place value; 0.125 is 125 thousandths and 0.13 is 130 thousandths, so 0.125 < 0.13.
She should compare only the first digit after the point, and since both are 1, the numbers are equal.
She is wrong because a decimal with a 5 in the thousandths place is always the smaller one.
questions.explain: Compare decimals by matching place values: 0.13 = 0.130, so 125 thousandths is less than 130 thousandths and 0.125 < 0.13. The trap Priya fell into is reading the digits after the point as whole numbers, which makes a longer decimal look bigger.

questions.question: On a drive through Nanaimo, a family checks four gas stations. Station A charges $1.759 per litre, station B charges $1.76 per litre, station C charges $1.749 per litre and station D charges $1.8 per litre. Which station has the LOWEST price per litre?
options: Station B, $1.76 per litre
Station D, $1.8 per litre, because it has the fewest digits
Station C, $1.749 per litre
Station A, $1.759 per litre
questions.explain: Write each price to thousandths first: 1.759, 1.760, 1.749, 1.800, then compare place by place, so $1.749 is the lowest. The trap is judging by how many digits a price has instead of by place value, since $1.8 is really $1.800, the highest price of all.

questions.question: At a Victoria school long jump, the results were Maya 2.45 m, Leo 2.5 m, Sofia 2.407 m and Tom 2.409 m. Ribbons go to the two LONGEST jumps. Who gets the ribbons?
options: Sofia (2.407 m) and Tom (2.409 m)
Leo (2.5 m) and Tom (2.409 m)
Maya (2.45 m) and Tom (2.409 m)
Leo (2.5 m) and Maya (2.45 m)
questions.explain: Rewrite each jump to thousandths: 2.500, 2.450, 2.409, 2.407, then take the two greatest, so Leo and Maya get the ribbons. The trap is choosing 2.407 and 2.409 because they have the most digits, when the hundredths place already puts them behind 2.45 and 2.5.
